claim: pyright reportPossiblyUnbound: "cv2" is possibly unbound at core/renderer.py:323-333 and core/image_utils.py:98 (10 sites)
rationale: cv2 is imported in a try/except ImportError block that sets _HAS_CV2 (core/image_utils.py:8-12, core/renderer.py same pattern). Every use site is inside an `if _HAS_CV2:` branch (core/renderer.py:320, core/image_utils.py:94), with a PIL fallback in the else. The checker cannot correlate the boolean flag with the import binding. No runtime NameError is reachable.

claim: mypy union-attr (32 sites) / pyright reportOptionalMemberAccess (35 sites): Item "None" of "QMenu | Any | None" has no attribute ... across ui/main_window.py
rationale: PyQt6 stubs annotate accessors such as menuBar(), layout() and addMenu() as Optional because the C++ API can return null before the widget is constructed. In this code every call site is on a widget the same method just created or on a QMainWindow whose menuBar() is auto-created on first access, so None is not reachable. Suppressing each site would need ~35 asserts or casts that change no behaviour.

claim: vulture: unused attribute 'max_redirects' (api/base.py:62), unused attribute 'MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS' (main.py:18), unused method 'paintEvent' (ui/preview_widget.py:45), unused variables 'wheel_url' (api/screenscraper.py:23), 'release_date' and 'clearlogo_url' (api/thegamesdb.py:15,18)
rationale: All six are live. max_redirects and MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS are assignments into third-party objects (requests.Session, PIL.Image) that the library reads — both are named security requirements in CLAUDE.md (redirect cap, decompression-bomb limit); deleting either weakens the app. paintEvent is a Qt event handler called by the framework, never by name. wheel_url/release_date/clearlogo_url are dataclass fields populated from API responses and part of the result contract. Vulture cannot see framework dispatch or library attribute reads.

claim: pyright reportIncompatibleMethodOverride: closeEvent (ui/main_window.py:560), paintEvent and resizeEvent (ui/preview_widget.py:45,113) override QWidget incompatibly
rationale: All three take an untyped `event` parameter where the PyQt6 stub declares a specific Optional event class. Python does not enforce parameter types at dispatch, and Qt passes the correct concrete event object. The only "fix" is to restate the stub's annotation, which changes no behaviour and would need re-editing whenever the stubs move.

claim: mypy arg-type/call-overload at core/renderer.py:327-329 (np.float32 on a list of tuples; getPerspectiveTransform overload), core/image_utils.py:292,300,301 (band_means rebound from list to ndarray), ui/workers.py:155 (**dict[str, object] to BoxRenderer)
rationale: Each is a stub-narrowing artifact, not a defect. np.float32(list_of_tuples) is the documented way to build a point array for cv2.getPerspectiveTransform and is what OpenCV's own examples use; the numpy stub declares only the scalar overload. band_means is deliberately built as a list then replaced by np.array(band_means) at core/image_utils.py:292 — the checker keeps the list type for the name. workers.py:155 splats a settings dict whose values are heterogeneous by design; mypy widens to object and reports one error per parameter type.
